report.source_text: After a week, the patient was referred for an Ophthalmology consult with complaints of ocular pain and redness and visual complaints. On ophthalmic examination, visual acuity in both eyes was 20/25. There was diffuse conjunctival injection bilaterally which was more prominent in the right eye. The conjunctional injection was a mixture of ciliary injection, episcleritis and conjunctivitis but more severe in the ciliary area. Neither eye had signs of intraocular inflammation. Pupillary light reflexes were sluggish bilaterally but no afferent pupillary defect was present. The patient was orthophoric without any muscle involvement and there was no diplopia. On funduscopy, there was bilateral optic disc swelling along with retinal hyperemia (optic disc hyperemia and vascular tortuosity) and diffuse intraretinal hemorrhage [Figure 1]. Intraocular pressure (IOP) was 26 mmHg in the right eye and 24 mmHg in the left eye. The patient was hospitalized with a probable diagnosis of ocular brucellosis and was treated with co-trimoxazole adult two tablets, three times a day (tid), rifampin 600 mg/day doxycycline 100 mg/BID and prednisolone 1 mg/kg for 2 months.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 29-year-old male presented in summer 2008 to the Infectious Disease Clinic of Hamadan Sina Hospital with acute onset fever (39°C), headache, malaise, sweating, and low back pain. Initial physical examination showed no organomegaly. Laboratory workup on admission revealed elevated WBC (13,350 with 85% neutrophils), elevated ESR (48 mm/h), positive CRP, and diagnostic Wright's agglutination titer of 1/1280, confirming brucellosis. Blood cultures were negative. Serology for syphilis, hepatitis, tuberculosis, and AIDS were negative. Lumbar puncture, electrolytes, ECG, and chest X-ray were normal. One week after admission, the patient developed ocular manifestations including bilateral conjunctival injection (more prominent on right), episcleritis, conjunctivitis, optic disc swelling, retinal hyperemia, intraretinal hemorrhage, elevated intraocular pressure (26 mmHg OD, 24 mmHg OS), and visual field limitation on perimetry. Brain and optic nerve imaging (CT and MRI) were unremarkable. The patient was diagnosed with ocular brucellosis and treated with co-trimoxazole (2 tablets three times daily), rifampin 600 mg/day, doxycycline 100 mg twice daily, and prednisolone 1 mg/kg for 2 months. Clinical response was documented: fever and headache resolved within 48 hours; visual acuity improved to 20/20 within one week; intraocular pressure normalized (19 mmHg OD, 16 mmHg OS with timolol); optic disc swelling and hyperemia decreased by 4 weeks with IOP within normal limits bilaterally. At 13 months after treatment completion, funduscopic examination was normal, indicating complete resolution of ocular manifestations.
